mergedParams.userDescription: Luma key fades and alpha matte reveals. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Luma Key & Alpha Matte Reveals for Text/Video/Images

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'LumaKeyReveal' that simulates a luma key fade effect for revealing text, images, or video content. The effect should animate opacity based on a luminance threshold pattern, creating a cinematic reveal where brighter areas appear first, followed by mid-tones and shadows. Use generic AnimationRange effects with multiple keyframes to create a stepped opacity reveal that mimics professional video luma keying. The effect should accept parameters for reveal duration (default 1.5s), threshold steps (3-5 levels), and direction (bright-to-dark or dark-to-bright). Implement as a provider-mode effect that targets components by ID, using opacity animations with custom easing curves between threshold steps. The reveal should feel organic and film-like, as if the content is emerging from or dissolving into light.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Create stepped opacity animations with 5 keyframes: [{prog: 0, val: 0}, {prog: 0.2, val: 0.3}, {prog: 0.4, val: 0.6}, {prog: 0.7, val: 0.85}, {prog: 1, val: 1}] for bright-to-dark mode. Use 'ease-in-out' easing between steps. Input params: duration (number, default 1500ms), direction ('brightFirst' | 'darkFirst'), thresholdSteps (3-5), targetIds (string[]). Return format: { effects: [{ type: 'opacity', mode: 'provider', targetIds, start: 0, duration, easing: 'ease-in-out', ranges }] }. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'AlphaMattePeel' that creates a directional alpha matte reveal effect, simulating the classic video editing technique where content is revealed through an animated matte layer. The effect should combine transform (translateX/Y) and opacity animations to create a peeling or wiping reveal from any direction (top, bottom, left, right, diagonal). Use mask-like opacity gradients by animating multiple transform properties simultaneously - the content should slide in slightly while fading, creating depth and dimensionality. Accept parameters for peel direction, reveal duration, offset distance (how far the content moves during reveal), and blur amount for soft edges. The effect should support both linear and curved peel patterns using different easing functions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (combined AnimationRange[]). Return multiple effects: opacity + translateX/Y + optional blur. For left-to-right peel: translateX ranges [{prog: 0, val: -50}, {prog: 1, val: 0}], opacity [{prog: 0, val: 0}, {prog: 0.3, val: 0.8}, {prog: 1, val: 1}], blur [{prog: 0, val: 4}, {prog: 0.7, val: 0}]. Input params: direction (enum: 'left' | 'right' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'diagonal-tl' | 'diagonal-br'), duration (default 1200ms), offset (default 50px), softness (blur 0-10px), targetIds. Use 'ease-out' for transforms, 'ease-in-out' for opacity. Return: { effects: [opacityEffect, transformXEffect, transformYEffect, blurEffect].filter(Boolean) }.

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'ChromaKeyDissolve' that mimics professional chroma key compositing effects for text and media transitions. The effect should create a color-based dissolve where specific color channels (R, G, B) fade at different rates, creating a prismatic or channel-separation effect during the transition. Combine opacity, color filters, and subtle scale animations to achieve the chroma key aesthetic. The effect should support both fade-in and fade-out modes, with parameters for channel delay (time offset between R, G, B channels), color shift intensity, and whether to include chromatic aberration via translateX/Y micro-offsets. Perfect for creating retro video effects or modern glitch-style reveals.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (combined). Create separate effects for each color channel using CSS filters. Red channel: filter 'sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(290deg)', Green: 'sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(100deg)', Blue: 'sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(200deg)'. Stagger opacity for each with channelDelay offset. Add micro transforms: translateX [{prog: 0, val: -2}, {prog: 0.5, val: 2}, {prog: 1, val: 0}] for aberration. Input params: mode ('in' | 'out'), duration (1000ms), channelDelay (50-200ms), aberrationAmount (0-5px), targetIds. Return array of effects with staggered start times based on channelDelay.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal waveform effect preset called 'AudioMatteReveal' that uses audio analysis to drive an alpha matte-style reveal. The effect should react to bass frequencies to control opacity reveals, creating a pulsing, music-driven appearance effect. Unlike simple beat reactions, this should accumulate opacity over time - each bass hit adds to the reveal progress, eventually fully revealing the content. Include parameters for sensitivity threshold, accumulation rate (how much each beat adds), decay rate (slight fade back between beats), and frequency range selection (bass, mid, or treble). The reveal should feel organic and musical, as if the content is being painted on by the audio waveform.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (audio-reactive). Use accumulator pattern with waveform data. Configuration: { type: 'custom', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: 0.7, threshold: 0.5, accumulate: true, accumulationRate: 0.1, decayRate: 0.02 }. Implement custom effect logic that tracks accumulated opacity value, adding accumulationRate when bass > threshold, subtracting decayRate otherwise. Clamp between 0-1. Input params: frequencyBand ('bass' | 'mid' | 'treble'), sensitivity (0-1), accumRate (0.05-0.2), decay (0-0.05), targetIds. Return: { effects: [{ type: 'waveform', mode: 'provider', targetIds, waveformEffect: config }] }. Requires useWaveformData hook.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'GradientMatteWipe' that creates sophisticated gradient-based matte transitions for revealing content. Instead of simple linear wipes, use multiple overlapping gradient zones with different timing offsets to create organic, flowing reveals. The effect should animate opacity using a virtual gradient matte that moves across the content - imagine a soft-edged gradient sliding across the element, revealing it progressively. Support radial and linear gradient patterns, with parameters for gradient angle, softness (gradient spread), number of gradient steps, and wave pattern (straight, curved, or zigzag edge). Include subtle scale and blur animations that follow the gradient edge for added depth.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (complex AnimationRange[]). Simulate gradient matte using multiple opacity keyframes with calculated prog values based on position. For 5-step gradient at 45° angle: create 5 opacity effects with staggered timing. Each zone: [{prog: 0, val: 0}, {prog: zoneStart, val: 0}, {prog: zoneMiddle, val: 1}, {prog: 1, val: 1}]. Add coordinated blur: [{prog: 0, val: 8}, {prog: 0.5, val: 2}, {prog: 1, val: 0}] and scale: [{prog: 0, val: 0.95}, {prog: 1, val: 1}]. Input params: pattern ('linear' | 'radial'), angle (0-360), steps (3-10), softness (0.1-0.5), duration, targetIds. Calculate zone positions based on angle and steps.

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'DepthMatteReveal' that simulates Z-depth based alpha matte effects, where content appears to emerge from or recede into different depth layers. Combine scale, blur, and opacity animations to create a convincing depth-of-field reveal effect. Content should start small and blurred (as if far away), then scale up while coming into focus and gaining opacity. Support multiple depth layers with staggered timing, creating a parallax-like reveal. Parameters should include number of depth layers, depth range (how much scale difference), focus range (blur amount), and whether to reverse the effect for depth-based concealment.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (combined depth simulation). For 3-layer depth: Layer 1 (back): scale [0.7→1], blur [12→0], opacity [0→1] over duration*1.2. Layer 2 (mid): scale [0.85→1], blur [6→0], opacity [0→1] over duration. Layer 3 (front): scale [0.95→1], blur [2→0], opacity [0→1] over duration*0.8. Use 'ease-out' for scale, 'ease-in-out' for blur/opacity. Input params: layers (1-5), depthRange (0.5-1.5 scale multiplier), maxBlur (5-20px), staggerDelay (50-200ms), reverse (boolean), targetIds. Return effects array with calculated start offsets for each layer.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'FilmBurnReveal' that mimics the organic reveal patterns of film burns and light leaks used in vintage video editing. The effect should create irregular, organic opacity reveals with fluctuating brightness and color temperature shifts. Use complex AnimationRange patterns with multiple random-like keyframes to simulate the unpredictable nature of film burns. Include flickering opacity, warm color overlays (orange/yellow tints), and dynamic brightness pulses. Parameters for burn intensity, flicker rate, color temperature (warm to cool), and whether to include film grain texture effects via rapid micro-scale animations.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (complex organic). Create flickering opacity with 8-10 keyframes: [{prog: 0, val: 0}, {prog: 0.1, val: 0.3}, {prog: 0.15, val: 0.2}, {prog: 0.3, val: 0.7}, {prog: 0.35, val: 0.6}, ...]. Add brightness filter: values oscillating between 1.0-1.5. Color filter using sepia/hue-rotate for warmth. Micro-scale for grain: [{prog: 0, val: 1}, {prog: 0.1, val: 1.01}, {prog: 0.2, val: 0.99}, ...] with 20ms segments. Input params: intensity (0.5-2), flickerRate (5-20 flickers), warmth (0-100 for hue), includeGrain (boolean), duration, targetIds. Use 'linear' easing for flicker realism.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal waveform effect preset called 'FrequencyMatte' that uses different frequency bands to control different aspects of a matte reveal. Bass frequencies control overall opacity, mids control edge softness (blur), and trebles add shimmer effects (brief opacity spikes). This creates a rich, multi-layered audio-reactive reveal where the full frequency spectrum contributes to the effect. The matte should build up over time with audio input, creating an accumulative reveal that responds to the music's full dynamic range. Include parameters for frequency sensitivity per band, accumulation vs real-time mode, and visual feedback intensity.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (multi-band). Return array of three waveform effects: 1) Bass→Opacity: { type: 'opacity', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: 0.8, accumulate: true }. 2) Mid→Blur: { type: 'blur', audioProperty: 'mid', sensitivity: 0.6, minValue: 0, maxValue: 4 }. 3) Treble→Brightness: { type: 'brightness', audioProperty: 'treble', sensitivity: 0.9, minValue: 1, maxValue: 1.3, responseTime: 50 }. Input params: bassSensitivity, midSensitivity, trebleSensitivity (all 0-1), accumulate (boolean), smoothing (0-500ms), targetIds. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects', dependencies: { presets: ['waveformData'] } }.

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'MaskEdgeReveal' that focuses on revealing content through animated edge detection masks. The effect should create the illusion that only the edges or outlines of content appear first, followed by the fill. Achieve this using a combination of CSS filters (contrast, brightness) and opacity animations that simulate edge detection algorithms. Start with high contrast and low brightness to show edges only, then gradually normalize values while increasing opacity. Include parameters for edge thickness, reveal sequence (edges-first vs fill-first), and whether to include a scanning line effect that moves across the content during reveal.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (filter-based edge simulation). Phase 1 (edges): filter 'contrast(5) brightness(0.2)', opacity 0.5. Phase 2 (transition): filter 'contrast(2) brightness(0.6)', opacity 0.8. Phase 3 (full): filter 'contrast(1) brightness(1)', opacity 1. Add optional scan line via linear gradient background animated with translateY. Input params: edgeThickness (via contrast 3-10), sequence ('edgeFirst' | 'fillFirst' | 'simultaneous'), includeScan (boolean), scanSpeed (500-2000ms), duration, targetIds. Return combined effects array with calculated phase timings. Use 'ease-in-out' for smooth filter transitions.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'DataMoshing' that simulates digital video compression artifacts and data moshing effects popular in glitch art. The effect should create a reveal that looks like corrupted video data is being reconstructed - with block artifacts, color channel shifts, and temporal displacement effects. Use a combination of pixelation (via scale and image-rendering), RGB channel separation (via translateX/Y offsets), and stuttering opacity reveals to achieve the data mosh aesthetic. Parameters should control corruption intensity, block size, channel displacement amount, and whether to include compression artifact colors (green/purple tints).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (glitch composite). Create blocky reveal using scale with image-rendering: [{prog: 0, val: 0.125}, {prog: 0.3, val: 0.25}, {prog: 0.6, val: 0.5}, {prog: 1, val: 1}] with CSS image-rendering: pixelated. RGB separation via 3 transform effects with offsets: R: translateX(-3→0), G: translateY(-3→0), B: translateX(3→0). Stutter opacity: [0, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.6, 1] over 6 keyframes. Add corruption colors via hue-rotate filter animating 0→180→0. Input params: glitchIntensity (0.5-2), blockSize (via scale steps), channelSplit (1-10px), includeColors (boolean), duration, targetIds. Return all effects with matching duration but offset starts for desync effect.
